name: Primary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood Due to Alveolar Vascular Disorder
aliases: Alveolar Vascular Disorder-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
Primary Childhood and Adult Interstitial Lung Disease with Alveolar Vascular Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Interstitial Lung Disease due to Alveolar Vascular Disorder

criteria.description: Progressive exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough persisting for more than 3 months
High-resolution CT showing diffuse interstitial infiltrates with alveolar septal thickening and vascular abnormalities
Lung biopsy demonstrating alveolar capillary dysplasia or vascular remodeling with interstitial fibrosis
Restrictive ventilatory defect with decreased diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)
Exclusion of secondary interstitial lung diseases such as connective tissue disease or environmental exposures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all major criteria including clinical presentation, characteristic imaging, histopathology, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory; multidisciplinary evaluation recommended.

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.symptomName: Hypoxemia at rest or with exertion
searchTerms: low oxygen levels at rest or exercise
chronic fatigue due to poor oxygenation
feeling weak from long-term low oxygen

common.symptomName: Bibasilar inspiratory crackles on lung auscultation

searchTerms: symptoms of high lung blood pressure
breathlessness and syncope from lung pressure

rare.symptomName: Weight loss due to chronic illness

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory alkalosis
Elevated serum biomarkers of fibrosis (e.g., KL-6, SP-D) in some cases
imaging: High-resolution CT demonstrating diffuse interstitial infiltrates, alveolar septal thickening, and vascular abnormalities
Echocardiography showing signs of pulmonary hypertension in advanced cases
genetic: Mutations in genes related to alveolar capillary development (e.g., FOXF1) reported in some patients
other: Lung biopsy revealing alveolar capillary dysplasia with misalignment of pulmonary veins and interstitial fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Usual interstitial pneumonia pattern on imaging

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
